citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
Daily observation of a cream colored ram was not done sufficiently to assess his health and well-being. The ram was
found with the right horn wedged onto and digging into the flesh of his right cheek, under the right eye. The area in front
as well as behind the horn was hairless. Dried crusty blackish/red blood could be seen along both intersecting sections of
the horn with the skin. An employee was not able to pry the horn away from the cheek to better evaluate the full extent of
the injury beneath. Failure to promptly identify such conditions delays treatment and causes undue animal pain and
distress. The licensee must ensure that daily observation of all animals occurs in order to assess their health and well-
being. Timely communication with the attending veterinarian must occur to provide proper diagnosis and medical
attention. In consultation with the attending veterinarian, a treatment plan must be established for the ram. Correct by
09/21/2026.

The outdoor enclosure for the capybara is not enclosed by a continuous 6 feet tall perimeter fence on all sides. The lack
of an adequate perimeter fence presents a safety risk to the animals within the facility in that there isn’t an adequate
secondary containment system to hold animals that may escape their primary enclosures or a sufficient barrier to keep
animals and unauthorized persons out. The facility must ensure that the capybara outdoor primary enclosure is enclosed
by a 6-foot perimeter fence at least 3 feet in distance from the primary enclosure. Correct by 10/09/2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
